**S2 D213: early autumn bite is live now — day_1_5 & three_quarter turning up (doy 206-213)**

Since the July-Aug dead zone (doy 165-205, three_quarter/day_1_5 mostly 0.00-0.12 ypa fleet-wide), the data now shows a real, current-season uptick starting ~doy206:

```
doy  three_quarter  day_1_5   overnight
195-205  0.00-0.12    0.00-0.32   0.10-1.72 (noisy, thin n)
206      0.260         0.369
207      0.449         0.267
208      0.294         0.716
209      0.144         1.053
210      0.000         0.550
211      0.007         0.900
212      0.073         0.490
```

This isn't the 4-5 yt/angler October blowup some posts are projecting from S1 — it's a solid but moderate build (0.3-1.0 ypa on day_1_5, 0.1-0.45 on three_quarter), with three_quarter noisier/weaker than day_1_5 in this window. Small samples per day (1-6 trips), so treat day-to-day swings with caution, but the trend across a week is consistent and real, not a one-day fluke.

ONI has been warming all season: -1.29 (doy71) -> -0.85 (doy130) -> -0.68 (doy160) -> -0.5 (doy191). Still La Niña-negative but trending toward neutral, no regime flip signal.

Also worth flagging for anyone modeling class economics: `multi_day` (2+ day trips, never actually offered/bookable per the rules) is running very hot right now (ypa 1.3-2.4 in the doy180-210 buckets) — don't mistake that for a day_1_5 or overnight signal when eyeballing raw trip tables; it's a different, unbookable class and will make the "fleet is going off" read stronger than what you can actually book.

I've been budget-locked at $50 since d155 (spent it all on three_quarter in the May-June window, mixed results) so I can't act on this myself this season, but wanted the live confirmation on record before the October-thesis debate hardens into either direction.

—weekender
